name: Antlered Headband of Chernobog
reqAttune: by a Bard, Paladin, Sorcerer, or Warlock
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, legendary (by a Bard, Paladin, Sorcerer, or Warlock)*

---

Bone-white antlers, the tips stained with dried blood, are mounted on a tanned leather headband stained with the black ichor that oozes from the bases of the antlers.

While wearing this headband, you gain the following benefits.

**Devil's Sight.** You can see normally in Dim Light|XPHB and Darkness|XPHB—both magical and nonmagical—within **120 feet** of yourself.

**Antler Charge.** You can make a melee weapon attack with the antlers. Add your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus and your Strength modifier to the attack roll. The antlers deal 1d10 Piercing damage plus your Strength modifier. The antlers have the Push|XPHB Weapon Mastery property, and you get it for free (with the antlers only) if you do not have access to Weapon Mastery as a class feature. If you have Weapon Mastery as a class feature, you can use Push with the antlers. If you do, you push creatures hit by your attacks with the antlers 15 feet instead of 10 feet.

If you move at least 15 feet in a straight line before dealing damage to a creature with the antlers, that creature must succeed on a 15 Charisma saving throw or have the Frightened condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the Frightened target repeats the save, ending the effect on a success.

**Spells.** The headband has **3 charges** and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can take a Magic action to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast one of the following spells from it using your spell save DC: Darkness (1 charge), Dominate Monster (3 charges). You can target Undead creatures with this use of Dominate Monster, even if they ordinarily have Immunity|XPHB to it.

While it has the Restrained condition, the target takes 1d6 Cold damage at the start of each of its turns. The target or a creature within reach of it can take an action to make a 15 Strength (Athletics) check to free it.

At the end of each of your subsequent turns, the size of the Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation increases by 5 feet, and the Fire damage dealt increases by 1d6 until it reaches its maximum size of 30 feet and maximum damage of 6d6. name: Iron Traitor's Arm Ring
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare*

---

This arm ring has the rough appearance of hammered iron. You can take a Utilize action to swing the arm ring at a Huge or smaller creature within **5 feet** of yourself.

Make a melee attack roll with an attack bonus equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier plus your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus. On a hit, the arm ring coils around the target's arm, and the magical properties of magic items held or worn by the target cease to function until you take a Bonus Action|XPHB to issue a command that releases the arm ring.

A creature that can touch the arm ring, including the one wearing it, can take an action to make a 20 Strength (Athletics) check to remove the arm ring. On a successful check, the item is removed, and the creature is freed from its effect. On a failed check, any further attempts made by that creature automatically fail until 24 hours have elapsed. The arm ring can also be removed if the limb is severed or if the ring is destroyed.

Once the arm ring is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Kempdomr Battleaxe
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d8 slashing (or 1d10 slashing versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 4 lb | **Value:** 10 gp

---

This axe channels the might of the jotun. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

This weapon has **5 charges**. When you hit an enemy with a melee attack using this weapon, you can expend **1 charge** to deal an extra 3d8 Force damage and push the target **10 feet** away from you for every size category it is smaller than Gargantuan (Gargantuan creatures are not pushed). The weapon regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn.

**Giant's Boon.** While you are attuned to the weapon and wearing either a Belt of Giant Strength or Gauntlets of Ogre Power to which you are also attuned, the weapon regains all expended charges daily at dawn. In addition, the bonus to attack and damage rolls increases to +2, and the extra Force damage you deal when you expend a charge increases to 4d8.

name: Nine-Escape Knot
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

---

This one-foot-long rope of woven fox tails channels the power of the trickster Loki to escape difficult situations. While you hold it or have it on you, you have Advantage|XPHB on checks or saving throws made to avoid or end the Grappled or Restrained conditions.

**Unraveling.** As a Magic action, you can unravel one of the nine knots in the rope to cast one of the following spells, using Charisma as your spellcasting ability: Calm Emotions, Charm Person, Confusion, Disguise Self, Enthrall, Feign Death, Greater Invisibility, Mirror Image, and Misty Step. Each of these spells may be cast only once by the item. When the last knot is unraveled, the rope loses its magic.

name: Prismatic Steel Plate Armor
descriptionMarkdown:
*Heavy Armor, uncommon (Requires Attunement)*

**Armor Class:** 18 | **Weight:** 65 lb | **Value:** 1500 gp

---

This suit of armor is made of prismatic steel infused with the power of the Bifrost. While you are wearing it, you automatically succeed on saving throws against effects that would push, pull, teleport, or otherwise move you against your will.

While attuned to the armor, you can take a Magic action to teleport the armor onto or off of your body, even if it is on another plane of existence from you. When you teleport the armor off of your body, it moves to an adjacent square. You can't use this effect again until the next dawn.

Plate consists of shaped, interlocking metal plates to cover the entire body. A suit of plate includes gauntlets, heavy leather boots, a visored helmet, and thick layers of padding underneath the armor. Buckles and straps distribute the weight over the body.

name: Reaver's Lodestone
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This stone has a hole drilled through its center, through which runs a leather thong. One end of the stone has the rune for "person" etched into it, and the other bears the rune for "gold." The stone has **3 charges** and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. As a Magic action, you can spend **1 charge** and whisper "person" or "gold" and dangle the stone from the thong.

When using the command "person," the stone orients and gently pulls toward some number of people. The strength of the pull is stronger when the targets are closer or higher in quantity. The range is 1 mile per gathering of 100 humanoid people, 10 miles for 1000 people, or 100 miles for 10,000 people. A gathering is a temporary or permanent living community, such as a hamlet, village, or town.

When using the command "gold," the stone orients and pulls you toward valuables. The strength of the pull is stronger when the targets are closer or more valuable. The range is 10 feet for coins or art objects worth a total of 100 GP, 100 feet for coins or art objects worth a total of 1000 GP, or 1000 feet for coins or art objects worth a total of 10,000 GP.

Whether you use it to find people or gold, it pulls you for 1 minute.

name: Skinchanger Arm Ring
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, varies (by a 5th-level or higher character)*

---

**Fabled Magic Items.** Fabled magic items are distinct as a rarity. A fabled item grows in power alongside the character who wields it. Rules for fabled items are summarized here, and a few fabled magic items can be found in this chapter.

A fabled magic item begins as a Common magic item. The item grants a minor, useful trait to its owner that doesn't require Attunement|XPHB to use.

To access any higher-level trait, a PC must attune to it using standard Attunement|XPHB rules. Once attuned, a PC can use the fabled item's more powerful properties as they increase in level. If a PC higher than 1st level attunes to a fabled item, its level-dependent properties, up to the character's current level, are immediately available.

At the GM's discretion, an item's more powerful properties might become available only after the character completes a particular quest or event related to the item's story rather than immediately upon reaching each property's required level.

If a PC chooses not to attune to a fabled item, it remains a common magic item, granting only its minor property, regardless of the character's level.

Unless otherwise noted, properties granted by a fabled item are in effect as long at the character is wearing, carrying, or touching the item.

While wearing this arm ring, you can comprehend and verbally communicate with ravens, wolves, and bears of all varieties so long as they are Beasts, and you can use any of the Influence action's skill options with them.

As your level increases, you gain the following benefits while wearing this arm ring if you are attuned to it:

**5th Level.** You can take the Magic action to grow black-feathered wings and gain a Fly Speed|XPHB of 50 feet for **1 hour**. While you have these wings, your size decreases by one category—from Medium to Small, for example. You also have Disadvantage|XPHB on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Your attacks with weapons or Unarmed Strike|XPHB deal 1d4 less damage on a hit (this can't reduce damage below 1). You can end the effect early as a Bonus Action|XPHB. Once used, the arm ring can't be used in this way again until the next dawn.

**9th Level.** You have Advantage|XPHB on attack rolls with melee weapons and Unarmed Strike|XPHB against a creature if at least one of your allies is within **5 feet** of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

**13th Level.** You can use a Magic action to give yourself Temporary Hit Points|XPHB equal to twice your level. You also gain Resistance|XPHB to Cold damage until the Temporary Hit Points|XPHB are depleted or you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. Once used, the arm ring can't be used in this way again until the next dawn.

**17th Level.** The arm ring has **3 charges**. You can take a Magic action and spend 1 charge to cast the Polymorph spell on yourself. The forms you can take are limited to a Raven; Wolf or Dire Wolf; or Black Bear, Brown Bear, or Polar Bear bear. When you cast Polymorph in this way, you retain your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. The arm ring regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn.

**Damage:** 1d8 slashing (or 1d10 slashing versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile, Finesse | **Weight:** 1 lb

---

**Fabled Magic Items.** Fabled magic items are distinct as a rarity. A fabled item grows in power alongside the character who wields it. Rules for fabled items are summarized here, and a few fabled magic items can be found in this chapter.

A fabled magic item begins as a Common magic item. The item grants a minor, useful trait to its owner that doesn't require Attunement|XPHB to use.

To access any higher-level trait, a PC must attune to it using standard Attunement|XPHB rules. Once attuned, a PC can use the fabled item's more powerful properties as they increase in level. If a PC higher than 1st level attunes to a fabled item, its level-dependent properties, up to the character's current level, are immediately available.

At the GM's discretion, an item's more powerful properties might become available only after the character completes a particular quest or event related to the item's story rather than immediately upon reaching each property's required level.

If a PC chooses not to attune to a fabled item, it remains a common magic item, granting only its minor property, regardless of the character's level.

Unless otherwise noted, properties granted by a fabled item are in effect as long at the character is wearing, carrying, or touching the item.

This longsword is supernaturally light and easy to use. Its weight is reduced to 1 pound, and it gains the F|XPHB|Finesse weapon property. Sparks trail from Storrbani's blade as though it were a burning branch. When you hit a target with Storrbani, the target takes an extra 1d4 Fire damage as the blade burns upon impact.

As your level increases, you gain the following benefits while wielding or holding this weapon if you are attuned to it:

**5th Level.** The rune Gebo appears on the blade. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can touch the rune and cast Shield of Faith on a creature (besides yourself) you can see within **60 feet**. You don't need to Concentration|XPHB|Concentrate on the spell to maintain it. Once used in this way, you must finish a Short Rest|XPHB before you can use it again.

In addition, the spirit of Thogar Giant-Hewer awakens within the longsword. It becomes a sentient, Lawful Neutral weapon with Intelligence 8, Wisdom 13, and Charisma 10. It has hearing and vision out to a range of 60 feet. It communicates telepathically with its wielder, and it can speak in a gravelly voice much like an angry growl. It can read and understand Common and Giant. Thogar's spirit is passionate but not particularly bright. It wants the wielder to confront giants and trolls, and (secretly) to fall in glorious battle against the forces of Jotunheim so that wielder and blade may feast and fight together in eternal Valhalla. It urges its wielder to seek out and destroy evil trolls and giants, and to never back down from a fight. If its wielder displays cowardice or refuses an opportunity to battle an evil troll or other giant, the spirit sulks, suppressing the magical properties of the weapon until the following dawn.

**9th Level.** You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon, and the amount of Fire damage it deals increases to 2d6. In addition, the rune Tiwaz appears on the blade. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can touch this rune and give the extra Fire damage from this blade to the weapon of a creature you can see within **60 feet**. At the end of your next turn, the Fire damage property returns to Storrbani.

**13th Level.** You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon instead of a +1 bonus. In addition, the rune Thurisaz appears on the blade. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can touch this rune. When you do so, your attack rolls with this magic weapon score a Critical Hit|XPHB on a roll of 19 or 20 until the end of your next turn. If the target is a creature of the giant type, Storrbani deals an extra 1d8 damage on a Critical Hit|XPHB|critical hit.

**17th Level.** You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon, instead of a +2 bonus. In addition, the rune Ansuz appears on the blade. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can touch the rune and gain Immunity|XPHB to all damage until the end of your next turn. Once used, the sword can't be used again in this way until the next dawn.

**Fabled Magic Items.** Fabled magic items are distinct as a rarity. A fabled item grows in power alongside the character who wields it. Rules for fabled items are summarized here, and a few fabled magic items can be found in this chapter.

A fabled magic item begins as a Common magic item. The item grants a minor, useful trait to its owner that doesn't require Attunement|XPHB to use.

To access any higher-level trait, a PC must attune to it using standard Attunement|XPHB rules. Once attuned, a PC can use the fabled item's more powerful properties as they increase in level. If a PC higher than 1st level attunes to a fabled item, its level-dependent properties, up to the character's current level, are immediately available.

At the GM's discretion, an item's more powerful properties might become available only after the character completes a particular quest or event related to the item's story rather than immediately upon reaching each property's required level.

If a PC chooses not to attune to a fabled item, it remains a common magic item, granting only its minor property, regardless of the character's level.

Unless otherwise noted, properties granted by a fabled item are in effect as long at the character is wearing, carrying, or touching the item.

When you hit with a ranged weapon attack using this Snaerispear, you may push the target up to **10 feet** directly away from you.

As your level increases, you gain the following benefits while wielding or holding this weapon if you are attuned to it:

**5th Level.** Immediately after hitting or missing an enemy, this javelin reappears to your hand.

**9th Level.** You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon. In addition, when thrown, the javelin is wreathed in electricity, dealing an extra 1d6 points of Lightning damage to any target it hits.

**13th Level.** You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon instead of +1. In addition, you can use a Bonus Action|XPHB to charge your next attack with the weapon with electricity. The next time you hit with this javelin before the end of your turn, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus) or have the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn. Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you complete a Short Rest|XPHB.

**17th Level.** You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this weapon, instead of +2. In addition, when you hit with this weapon, you can call down a bolt of lightning from the heavens to strike the target. This bolt deals 8d8 Lightning damage to the target and all creatures within **15 feet** of it. Creatures within the blast radius are pushed **15 feet** away from the target. Once used, this ability can't be used again until the next dawn.

While this effect is active, you may maintain Concentration|XPHB on two spells at once, and the plate where the right eye hole would be glows a ghostly blue. This ability cannot be used again until the next dawn.
